column1: # clues.tsv for ft_recursive_power — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".
Every recursion needs a place to stop. What is the base case here — what should raising any number to the power of zero give? Note that even zero raised to the zeroth power follows this same rule.
Once the base case is settled, how is nb to the power p related to a smaller power of nb? Check that the sign comes out right when the base is negative.

What does a NEGATIVE exponent mean for an integer-only function — is there a valid integer result, or is this an error case? What does the subject say it returns, and does yours return it even for the most extreme negative power?
